author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list opens at the first page when a page below the first is requested
summary: A request for the owner list naming a page below the first is read as asking for the first page. The list opens as normal instead of showing the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner list naming a page below the first, when it runs, then the first page of matches is listed
given that same request, when the response is returned, then it is the normal owner list rather than the error page
given a page number of zero and given a negative page number, when either request runs, then both open the first page
given a request naming no page at all, when it runs, then the first page still opens
non_goals: the veterinarian directory's handling of a page below the first
a page number beyond the last page
a page value that is not a number
changing how many owners a page holds
notes: Scoped from the intake record at line 1; the owner recorded no decisions beyond the request. Scope held to the owner list, as asked. The same tolerance elsewhere, a page beyond the last, and a non-numeric page are undecided and recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md. PRD covers this as REQ-OWN-005 with edge cases 4 and 5 of Owner records.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The owner listing's paging already lives in OwnerController (docs/system-design.md#contracts row `OwnerController`), which converts the 1-based `page` request parameter to a 0-based PageRequest in the private helper findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (OwnerController.java:133-137). The defect is that conversion alone: PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) throws IllegalArgumentException for any page below 1, and the unhandled exception renders the error page. The slice needs no new type, package, or pattern - one normalization of the requested page at the controller's request-binding seam. Two design-doc edits accompany this block: REQ-OWN-005 joins the `OwnerController` Contracts row, and the Constants section records the owner/vet asymmetry as current state. No ADR: the product choice (tolerate rather than reject) is already recorded in docs/prd.md REQ-OWN-005, and the technical choice is contained by this slice. Basis for the covering-code claim is grep over OwnerController.java and VetController.java (no IDE oracle connected in this run) - the weaker basis, so the implementer should confirm the helper signature in source before editing.
integration_points: Framework transport: the existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) slice with MockMvc drives the real binding, dispatch, and view selection. MockMvc is the sanctioned framework stub for controller tests (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy); assert the 200 status and the owners/ownersList view rather than reaching past the transport.

Repository boundary: OwnerRepository. Reuse the @MockitoBean override already declared in OwnerControllerTests (OwnerControllerTests.java:70) and its existing findByLastNameStartingWith stubbing. Reason no real implementation or hand-written double: the class is a @WebMvcTest slice with no JPA context, and a second double form inside a class that already overrides the bean would split one fixture in two. No new stub is introduced by this slice.

Model contract with the view: addPaginationModel publishes `currentPage` to owners/ownersList. The normalized page, not the raw request parameter, must reach both the PageRequest and this model attribute, or the rendered pager reports page 0.

patterns.description: findPaginatedForOwnersLastName - the 1-based-to-0-based conversion that currently throws. processFindForm (line 95) passes the same `page` value to both this helper and addPaginationModel, so normalizing once where the parameter is read keeps the query and the model in agreement; normalizing inside the helper alone leaves currentPage at the raw value.

The vet listing's identical helper. Out of scope by the prd-entry's non-goals and PRD open question; leave it untouched. Do not extract a shared helper in this slice - that would be an unrequested refactor across two feature packages.

risks.risk: The normalization reads as a business rule added to a controller, which architecture-principles.md pattern catalog bars for new rules ('A new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing one').
risks.mitigation: Keep it request-parameter normalization, not a domain rule: the *Web controller* row's own 'binds the request' clause covers coercing a query parameter into a valid value before delegating. One expression at the parameter's read site, no repository change, no new type, nothing the domain would need to know.

risks.risk: Silent scope creep into VetController or into other out-of-range page values (beyond the last page, non-numeric).
risks.mitigation: docs/prd.md#open-questions leaves all three undecided and the prd-entry lists them as non-goals. Change owner-list behavior for pages below the first only.

risks.risk: A test that asserts only the HTTP status would pass against a fix that returns the wrong page.
risks.mitigation: Acceptance criterion 1 requires the first page of matches. Assert the view name and the listOwners/currentPage model content, per testing-principles.md assertion patterns, for both page=0 and a negative page.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Effort rating routine: the fix is a single coercion at a seam OwnerController already demonstrates, and the test additions extend an existing @WebMvcTest class with fixtures already in place. Vocabulary check against docs/ubiquitous-language.md: it defines no paging term, and none is introduced here - 'page' stays the HTTP request parameter's name, not a domain concept.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp a below-first owner-list page to the first page

blast_radius.note: Ten production lines in one method of OwnerController plus two doc edits; one module, no sensitive or security-surface paths, and the 52 test lines account for most of the 13 hunks.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do exactly what the description says: Math.max(requestedPage, FIRST_PAGE) runs once at the top and the normalized value feeds both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so query and pager cannot diverge; the parameter rename is made safe by the explicit request-param name attribute, which still matches every ownersList.html pager link, and behavior for page 1, pages beyond the last, and non-numeric pages is untouched.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized zero and negative test and the no-page test assert currentPage and listOwners rather than status alone, and both would fail against the unclamped code because PageRequest.of(-1) throws; the residual gap is that no test drives page 2, so an explicit-name binding regression above page one would go unnoticed, which is a pre-existing hole the rename slightly sharpens.

reviewer_hedging.note: code-quality, test, and doc reviewers all approved with empty findings and no recommendations; security-reviewer is null because the low-risk plan scoped it out for a range clamp on an already-bound int, which is expected rather than silence.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions; the diff matches the requirement's stated surface and the vet-listing asymmetry was recorded as a PRD open question instead of being silently fixed.

rationale: A single clamp at the request-binding seam, normalized once and used for both the query and the pager, with tests that fail against the old code and a unanimous clean roster. A glance at the four-line OwnerController hunk confirms it; no flagged coordinates need a close read.
